Go module `github.com/bide-ai/bide`; [all packages](index.md).

`github.com/bide-ai/bide/model/modeltest` · [pkg.go.dev](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/bide-ai/bide/model/modeltest) · Stability: **stable**

Package modeltest checks an HTTP-backed agent.Model against the streaming contract the agent loop relies on:

**Functions**

- `func CheckFinish(t testing.TB, f agent.Finish)`: CheckFinish checks the Finish a first-party adapter sends.
- `func CheckSSEPrefix(t testing.TB, streamSSE func(body io.ReadCloser, send func(agent.Emit) bool), body []byte, cut int)`: CheckSSEPrefix checks, on top of ReadSSE's properties for body and for its first cut bytes, that a response cut short is never a success that differs from the whole response's success: a connection that closes partway must not turn a truncated answer into a complete one.
- `func Run(t *testing.T, newModel func(baseURL string, client *http.Client) agent.Model, event func(i int) string)`: Run runs the checks.
- `func ToolConfig(t *testing.T, newModel func(baseURL string, client *http.Client) agent.Model)`: ToolConfig checks that the adapter refuses a tool setup every provider rejects with agent.ErrConfig, before it sends anything: a tool name outside \[a-zA-Z0-9\_-\] or longer than 64 characters, two tools with one name, and a tool choice that cannot be met (an unknown mode; "required" or "tool" with no tools declared; "tool" naming no tool or one not declared).
- `func ToolNames(t *testing.T, newModel func(baseURL string, client *http.Client) agent.Model, refused, accepted []string)`: ToolNames checks the adapter's own tool-name rule against names an MCP server may list (the MCP grammar is 1 to 128 of A-Z a-z 0-9 \_ - ., wider than every provider's): each name in refused must fail with agent.ErrConfig that quotes the name, before anything is sent, and each name in accepted must reach the provider.

## type SSEResult

```go
type SSEResult struct {
	Emits []agent.Emit
	Msg   agent.Message
	Usage agent.Usage
	Err   error
}
```

SSEResult is what an adapter's SSE reader made of one response body: every Emit it sent, in order, and the message, usage, and error a consumer reading them gets.

**Constructors and functions**

- `func ReadSSE(t testing.TB, streamSSE func(body io.ReadCloser, send func(agent.Emit) bool), body []byte) SSEResult`: ReadSSE runs an adapter's SSE reader (streamSSE, which reads body and sends each event through send) over body and checks the properties every response must keep, whatever its bytes:
